title: Sangat online
hook: online kirtan and study groups can help, with care
tomorrow: why would Guru Nanak bless a rude village to stay right where it was?

segments.voice: A week of seva and sangat. Seva for the earth, the creek as family. Serve together, no stranger. My seva, small enough to keep. Find your people, where the Name is spoken. Two is a sangat. And yesterday, kirtan at home, a harmonium out of the closet. Now a screen.
screen: `A WEEK OF SEVA AND SANGAT.` → `KIRTAN AT HOME.` → `NOW A SCREEN.`

segments.voice: Sunday night, ten o'clock. Jas sends a link: a video kirtan with her Friday group and a few cousins from three time zones. Simran joins from her bed with the lights off. Eight little squares, one person on a tabla, someone's cat walking across a keyboard. Then her phone buzzes. A meme. Then another. By the second shabad she realizes she's been in two group chats and zero kirtan.
screen: `EIGHT SQUARES, THREE TIME ZONES.` → `A CAT ON A KEYBOARD.` → `TWO GROUP CHATS, ZERO KIRTAN.`

segments.voice: So does a screen count? Go back to the test from this week, Ang 72: the true company is known where the one Name is spoken. That test doesn't ask for a room. Eight squares singing the same shabad can pass it. For someone two hours from a gurdwara, or too sick to leave the house, an online kirtan or study circle can be a real lifeline. But the test does ask for the Name to be heard, and a screen is built to pull you somewhere else. So some Sikhs who keep sangat online set a few guards. Notifications off. Camera on if the group wants it, a scarf or a covered head as you would in the hall. One tab open. And the screen doesn't replace everything: nobody can serve langar through a video call, or wipe a stranger's shoes. Simran turns her phone face down, joins the next line out loud, and Jas sees her lips moving and grins. Sangat anywhere, with care.
screen: `ANG 72 DOESN'T ASK FOR A ROOM.` · `A LIFELINE FOR THE FAR AND THE SICK.` · `GUARDS: ONE TAB, PHONE DOWN.` · `NO LANGAR THROUGH A SCREEN.` · then, large: `SANGAT ANYWHERE.`

segments.voice: A gratitude count. On one hand, count the people who were sangat for you this past week, in a room or on a screen, one finger for each, and say each name silently as you fold it down. If you run out of names, keep the hand open and wait.
Sangat online. Company where the Name is spoken, through a screen, kept with care: one tab, phone down.
This one goes with you: sangat anywhere, as long as the Name can be heard there. A week done.

howItsDone: Some gurdwaras stream the Hukamnama and kirtan, and Sikhs join online Sukhmani, Nitnem and study circles, alongside an in-person sangat when they can reach one.
